headline: A 2016 law lets members of Congress give Capitol-flown flags and sympathy certificates to families of people who died in the line of duty in public safety jobs.
what_it_does: The law allows a Representative or Senator to give a flag that has flown over the Capitol to the immediate family of a firefighter, police officer, rescue squad or ambulance crew member, or other public safety officer who died in the line of duty. The family must request the flag. The flag comes with a signed certificate that expresses sympathy for the family. The Speaker of the House or the President pro tempore of the Senate signs the certificate, along with the member giving the flag.
when_it_takes_effect: The law took effect when it was signed on May 16, 2016.
